                                                                                          Direct Testimony of Brandon Fortie
                                                                                                      PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                                            SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                                                Page 3 of 17
   1                                 PERSONAL INFORMATION

 2   Q. Please state your name and address.
 3   A. My name is Brandon Fortie. My address is 9109 Wedel Cemetery Road, Temple,
 4   Texas 76501.

 5   Q. Are you the same individual who filed a Motion to Intervene in this
 6   proceeding?
 7   A. Yes.

 8   Q. Please state your background.
 9   A. I purchased my property on April 28, 2021, and it is my primary residence. My family
10   and I live on the property full time. We purchased this property specifically because it
11   was rural residential property with open space and agricultural land around it. Since
12   purchasing the property, we have continued repairing and improving it as our long-term
13   homestead. Part of the property is used for residential purposes, and part is used for
14   cattle and agricultural activities. We actively use the property every day for normal rural
15   living, outdoor activities, storage, parking, cattle, and agricultural use.

16   Q. Are you testifying on behalf of yourself?
17   A. I am testifying on behalf of myself and my wife, Leslie Nichole

18   Q. Is your property affected by the proposed transmission line project?
19   A. Yes. My property identified as Parcel 3520 is located within Segment A2 and would
20   be directly affected by the proposed transmission line route.

21   Q. What is the purpose of your testimony?
22   A. The purpose of my testimony is to explain how the proposed Route A2 transmission
23   line would directly affect my occupied residence, agricultural use, future use of my
24   property, and the surrounding rural residential community. My primary concern is the
25   close proximity of the proposed transmission line to my full-time occupied home and the
26   failure to sufficiently minimize residential impacts within this area.

27   Q. What routes affect your property?
28   A. My property is affected by the Segment A2 routes identified in Oncor’s application.

29   Q. What routes do you oppose?
30   A. I oppose Route A2 because the proposed transmission line would be located
31   approximately 282 feet from my occupied residence on Parcel 3520. In my opinion,
32   routing a 765-kV transmission line this close to an occupied rural home does not
33   sufficiently minimize impacts to existing residential land use. The route would
34   permanently place large transmission structures directly adjacent to an established
35   homesite where my family lives every day. The area has already experienced


                                                                  Direct Testimony of Brandon Fortie
                                                                              PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                    SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                        Page 5 of 17
  1   substantial utility development, and this route would add another major utility corridor
 2   into an existing rural residential area.

 3   Q. What routes do you support, if any?
 4   A. I support Routes A3, A6, and C1 because, based on my understanding of the routing
 5   maps, those routes appear to follow or parallel existing transmission corridors and utility
 6   infrastructure to a greater extent than Route A2. Those routes also appear to pass
 7   between existing solar developments and utility areas instead of routing directly through
 8   established rural residential homesites like mine. In my opinion, those routes appear to
 9   create less impact to occupied residences and existing rural residential communities
10   than Route A2.

11   Q. Have you previously testified before the Public Utility Commission of Texas?
12   A. No.

13   Q. Was this testimony prepared by you or under your supervision?
14   A. Yes.

15                               DESCRIPTION AND LOCATION

16   Q. Do you have pictures that depict the property and how it is used?
17   A. Yes. See Exhibits 2-7. These include aerial maps, proximity measurements, nearby
18   infrastructure, and photographs of the property.

19   Q. Have the pictures been altered?
20   A. No, except for simple labels or markings used for clarity.

21   Q. Do the pictures accurately represent the views of the property?
22   A. Yes. The photographs accurately represent the current conditions of my property and
23   the views from my residence and surrounding areas.

24   Q. Please describe your property.
25   A. My property consists of approximately 3.65 acres identified as Parcel 3520. My family
26   and I live there full time. The property includes our occupied residence, open yard
27   areas, parking and storage areas, cattle use areas, and agricultural space that we
28   actively maintain and use on a daily basis. We spend a large amount of time outdoors
29   on the property because this is our home and rural homestead, not vacant land or
30   investment property. We regularly use the yard and outdoor areas for normal daily
31   activities, equipment storage, maintaining the property, working outside, and spending
32   time with family. The property also includes a private septic system and improvements
33   associated with rural residential living. Since purchasing the property in 2021, we have
34   continued making repairs and improvements and intend to continue using the property
35   as our long-term home.


                                                                     Direct Testimony of Brandon Fortie
                                                                                 PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                       SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                           Page 6 of 17
  1   Q. Approximately where is your property located within the study area?
 2   A. My property identified as Parcel 3520 is located within Segment A2 near Wedel
 3   Cemetery Road.

 4   Q. How close is the proposed transmission line to your home and improvements?
 5   A. Based on the routing information available to me, the proposed 765-kV transmission
 6   line would be located approximately 282 feet from my occupied home on Parcel 3520.
 7   That distance is extremely close for infrastructure of this size. My family lives there full
 8   time, and we use the yard, outdoor areas, driveway, and surrounding property every
 9   day. I can stand in my yard and clearly see the area where the proposed structures
10   would be located. The proposed line would not be off in the distance. It would be directly
11   adjacent to where we live every day. The transmission structures would remain visible
12   from the house, driveway, yard, and surrounding portions of the property and would
13   permanently change the environment surrounding our home. In my opinion, placing a
14   765-kV transmission line this close to an occupied residence does not minimize impacts
15   to existing residential land use.

16                           LAND USE, CONCERNS AND HISTORY

17   Q. Please describe how your property and surrounding properties are used.
18   A. The surrounding area is primarily rural residential and agricultural land. Families in
19   this area live on and actively use their properties for homes, cattle, farming, equipment
20   storage, trailers, outdoor activities, and other agricultural activities. The area contains
21   occupied residences, barns, fenced pasture areas, ponds, and agricultural
22   improvements. This is an established rural community where people actively live on and
23   use their land every day.

24   Q. Are there agricultural uses within this segment?
25   A. Yes. There are cattle operations, hay production activities, and other agricultural
26   uses throughout this segment.

27   Q. Are there existing energy or utility developments in your area?
28   A. Yes. There are already solar facilities, substations, and existing utility infrastructure
29   within the surrounding area. There is also an East Bell County Water Supply main line
30   running through portions of this area.

31   Q. Why is this relevant to the proposed transmission line?
32   A. This area has already experienced substantial utility and industrial development
33   compared to what previously existed in the community. Over the last several years, the
34   area around us has continued changing because of additional solar facilities, BESS
35   facilities, substations, and other utility infrastructure. My concern is that Route A2 would
36   continue concentrating large utility infrastructure directly around occupied homes and
37   rural residential property instead of following existing compatible utility corridors to a
38   greater extent.

                                                                    Direct Testimony of Brandon Fortie
                                                                                PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                      SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                          Page 7 of 17
  1   Q. What concerns do you have regarding routing the transmission line through
 2   this segment?
 3   A. My biggest concern is how close this line would be to my occupied home. This is not
 4   an undeveloped tract. It is where my family lives full time every day. I specifically chose
 5   this property because it was rural residential property with open space around it. We
 6   invested in this property and continued improving it because we intended for it to be our
 7   long-term home. Over the last several years, the area has already seen major utility
 8   development including substations, solar facilities, BESS facilities, and additional
 9   infrastructure. Now this proposed route would place a 765-kV transmission line
10   approximately 282 feet from my home. In my opinion, that places too much large utility
11   infrastructure into an established rural residential area and does not sufficiently
12   minimize impacts to occupied homes. I also do not believe it makes sense to route a
13   transmission line this close to existing homes when other routes appear to follow
14   existing transmission corridors and utility areas more closely.

15                                      FINANCIAL RISKS

16   Q. What do you think the financial risks will be to you?
17   A. I believe the proposed transmission line would negatively affect the long-term
18   desirability, enjoyment, and marketability of my property because the line would be
19   located approximately 282 feet from my occupied residence. In my opinion as the
20   property owner, many people looking for rural residential property would not want to live
21   this close to large 765-kV transmission structures. People purchase homes in this area
22   because it is rural and residential, not because they want to live immediately next to
23   major transmission infrastructure.

24   Q. What are the risks of devaluation of your property?
25   A. In my opinion, the close proximity of a major transmission corridor to my occupied
26   residence would reduce the residential appeal and desirability of the property. The
27   property was purchased and developed as a rural homesite, and the introduction of
28   large transmission structures approximately 282 feet from the home would permanently
29   change the character and perception of the property. I believe many future buyers
30   would view the proximity of the line to the home as a negative factor.

31                    HEALTH RISKS, ENVIRONMENTAL AND WILDLIFE

32   Q. What do you think are the health risks?
33   A. I have concerns about placing large high-voltage transmission infrastructure
34   approximately 282 feet from occupied residential homes where families live, work, and
35   spend time outdoors on a daily basis. My concern is based on the close residential
36   proximity and the long-term compatibility of this type of infrastructure within an
37   established rural residential setting.



                                                                  Direct Testimony of Brandon Fortie
                                                                              PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                    SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                        Page 8 of 17
  1   Q. What do you see as safety risks?
 2   A. I have concerns related to wildfire risks, equipment failure, severe weather events,
 3   and emergency response limitations in rural areas. This area relies heavily on volunteer
 4   fire response and rural access roads. I am also concerned about the risks associated
 5   with large transmission infrastructure being located close to homes, livestock areas, and
 6   agricultural operations. Because the proposed line would be located approximately 282
 7   feet from my occupied residence, any fire, storm damage, falling conductor, or
 8   equipment-related incident involving the line would occur in close proximity to homes
 9   and occupied rural property.

10   Q. What do you think will be the environmental impacts and risks?
11   A. Construction of the transmission line would disturb rural land that is currently used for
12   residential and agricultural purposes. Heavy construction equipment, access routes,
13   and transmission structure installation could affect drainage patterns, soil conditions,
14   and existing land use within the area.

15   Q. What do you think will be the risks to birds and native wildlife?
16   A. Wildlife currently uses this area because it still contains open rural land, ponds,
17   pasture areas, and undeveloped space. Additional transmission infrastructure and
18   construction activity would further disturb wildlife movement and habitat within the area.

19   Q. What do you think will be the risks to your agricultural activities and animals?
20   A. The transmission line could interfere with future agricultural improvements, fencing,
21   cattle movement, and daily agricultural activities on the property. Construction activity
22   and permanent utility infrastructure would also reduce the rural and agricultural
23   character of the area.

24   Q. What do you think will be the risks to your stock tanks and ground water?
25   A. I am concerned that construction activities and disturbance of the land could affect
26   drainage patterns and water movement in low-lying areas near the property.

27                 RECREATION, COMMUNITY VALUES AND AESTHETICS

28   Q. How would this transmission line affect your enjoyment of your property?
29   A. The proposed transmission line would permanently change the environment
30   surrounding my home because the structures and transmission corridor would be
31   located approximately 282 feet from my occupied residence. My family uses the outdoor
32   areas of the property daily, and the transmission line would become a constant visual
33   presence near our home. Instead of looking out onto open rural property, we would be
34   looking toward large transmission structures located very close to our residence.

35   Q. Do you think the proposed transmission line will affect any planned future use
36   on your land?


                                                                  Direct Testimony of Brandon Fortie
                                                                              PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                    SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                        Page 9 of 17
  1   A. Yes. It could interfere with future agricultural improvements, fencing, and planned
 2   use areas on the property.

 3   Q. How would this transmission line affect your rural community values for your
 4   area?
 5   A. The area has historically been rural residential and agricultural in nature. Additional
 6   utility infrastructure would continue changing the rural character of the surrounding
 7   community and reduce the open rural setting that originally attracted many families to
 8   this area.

 9   Q. How will this transmission line affect the aesthetic value of your property?
10   A. The proposed transmission structures would become one of the dominant visual
11   features surrounding my residence because of the close proximity to the home. Instead
12   of looking out onto a rural residential and agricultural landscape, the view from the
13   property would include large transmission infrastructure located approximately 282 feet
14   away. In my opinion, that is not compatible with the existing rural residential character of
15   the property or surrounding area.

16   Q. Do transmission routes parallel any existing rights of way on your property?
17   A. No.

18   Q. Does Oncor’s application properly identify the structures on your property?
19   A. To the best of my knowledge, the application does not fully reflect all current
20   residential and agricultural use occurring on and around the property.

21                        LOCAL ELECTRICITY SERVICE AND COSTS

22   Q. Do you think that this transmission line will improve your electric service in
23   your area?
24   A. I do not personally know whether it will improve electric service for my property.

25   Q. Do you think this transmission line will lower your electricity costs?
26   A. I do not believe it will lower my electricity costs.

27                         CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATION

28   Q. Is there anything else you would like to have considered in this proceeding?
29   A. I ask that the Commission carefully consider the close proximity of Route A2 to
30   occupied residences within this segment, including my home located approximately 282
31   feet from the proposed transmission line on Parcel 3520. My property is an actively
32   occupied rural homestead where my family lives every day. In my opinion, Route A2
33   does not sufficiently minimize impacts to existing residential land use or occupied
34   homes within this rural community. I also believe it is important to consider that other


                                                                  Direct Testimony of Brandon Fortie
                                                                              PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                    SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                       Page 10 of 17
 1   routes appear to parallel existing transmission corridors and utility infrastructure to a
2   greater extent rather than routing directly adjacent to established homesites like mine.

3   Q. Does this conclude your testimony?
4   A. Yes.

5

                                 LAND USE, CONCERNS AND HISTORY

        Q. Please describe how your property and surrounding properties are used.
        A. The surrounding area is primarily rural residential and agricultural land. Families in
        this area live on and actively use their properties for homes, cattle, farming, equipment
        storage, trailers, outdoor activities, and other agricultural activities. The area contains
        occupied residences, barns, fenced pasture areas, ponds, and agricultural
        improvements. This is an established rural community where people actively live on and
        use their land every day.

        Q. Are there agricultural uses within this segment?
        A. Yes. There are cattle operations, hay production activities, and other agricultural
        uses throughout this segment.

        Q. Are there existing energy or utility developments in your area?
        A. Yes. There are already solar facilities, substations, and existing utility infrastructure
        within the surrounding area. There is also an East Bell County Water Supply main line
        running through portions of this area.

        Q. Why is this relevant to the proposed transmission line?
        A. This area has already experienced substantial utility and industrial development
        compared to what previously existed in the community. Over the last several years, the
        area around us has continued changing because of additional solar facilities, BESS
        facilities, substations, and other utility infrastructure. My concern is that Route A2 would
        continue concentrating large utility infrastructure directly around occupied homes and
        rural residential property instead of following existing compatible utility corridors to a
        greater extent.
